ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, the upper node is labeled 10 V. On the left, there is a 4.7 kΩ resistor connected from the 10 V node to the middle base/voltage-regulation node; this node is connected downward through a Zener diode labeled 5.3 V to the lower common ground, and a downward 0.5 mA current is marked beside the Zener branch. On the right is the transistor branch: the collector is connected to 10 V through 220 Ω, the base is connected to the left middle node, and the emitter is connected to ground through a 470 Ω resistor. Reasoning: The Zener diode clamps the transistor base node at 5.3 V. The current through the 4.7 kΩ resistor is (10 - 5.3) / 4.7 kΩ = 4.7 V / 4.7 kΩ = 1 mA. The figure marks the Zener current as 0.5 mA, so from KCL at this node, the transistor base current can be obtained as IB = 1 mA - 0.5 mA = 0.5 mA. Given VBE = 0.6 V, therefore the emitter voltage VE = 5.3 - 0.6 = 4.7 V. The emitter resistor is 470 Ω, so the emitter current IE = 4.7 V / 470 Ω = 10 mA. For the BJT, IE = (β + 1)IB, therefore β + 1 = 10 mA / 0.5 mA = 20, hence β = 19.
